title: Chromosomes & sex determination
examples: How do chromosomes determine if a baby is a boy or a girl?
What is a karyotype and what does it show?
What happens if the sex chromosomes are not normal?

explain.say: Chromosomes are structures found inside the cell nucleus.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the DNA double helix. Look at the double helix, the backbone and the base pair. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Humans have a specific set of chromosomes that determine sex.
A karyotype is an organized picture of all the chromosomes.

items: XX or XY | Sex Chromosomes | Determines sex

explain.say: Females typically have two X chromosomes, represented as XX.

items: This combination is normal for females

explain.say: Males typically have one X and one Y chromosome, shown as XY.

items: XY: One X and one Y chromosome
This combination is normal for males

explain.say: In real life, doctors use karyotyping to check chromosome numbers.

faq.q: What are autosomes and sex chromosomes?
faq.a: Autosomes are the chromosomes that determine general body traits. Sex chromosomes are the specific pair, XX or XY, that determines biological sex.
asks: What do the non-sex chromosomes do?
Can you separate the body chromosomes from the sex ones?

faq.q: Does the presence of the Y chromosome always mean the baby is male?
faq.a: Yes, the presence of the Y chromosome is what typically signals male development. The X chromosome carries many genes important for both sexes.
asks: What is the role of the Y chromosome?
Is the Y chromosome the deciding factor for sex?

faq.q: What is the difference between XXY and normal sex chromosomes?
faq.a: XXY means there are three sex chromosomes, which is a condition called Klinefelter syndrome. Normal is either XX or XY.
asks: What happens with extra sex chromosomes?
Is having three sex chromosomes always a problem?

faq.q: Why are chromosomes so important for inheritance?
faq.a: Chromosomes carry our genes, which are the instructions for building and running our bodies. They are passed from parents to offspring.
asks: What is the job of the chromosomes?

faq.q: Can sex determination change during a person's life?
faq.a: No, the sex chromosomes are generally determined at conception and remain consistent throughout life. They are part of the basic genetic makeup.

facts: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes in total.
The first 22 pairs are called autosomes.
The 23rd pair consists of the sex chromosomes, X and Y.
Females usually have two X chromosomes (XX).

quiz.say: A karyotype analysis reveals the sex chromosomes are XX. What is the biological sex?
quiz.why: The XX combination is the standard genetic makeup for biological females.

wrong.0: This is wrong because males possess the Y chromosome, making their pairing XY.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the XX pairing is definitive for female sex determination.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the Y chromosome is absent in this specific XX pairing.

quiz.say: If a person has the sex chromosome combination XY, what is their biological sex?
quiz.why: The presence of the Y chromosome in the XY pairing determines the biological sex as male.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the Y chromosome provides the necessary genetic signal for maleness.
wrong.2: This is wrong because females are characterized by having two X chromosomes.
wrong.3: This is wrong because XY is the standard, expected pairing for male development.

quiz.say: Which set of chromosomes is responsible for determining biological sex?
quiz.why: The sex chromosomes, found in the 23rd pair, are specifically responsible for determining biological sex.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the Y chromosome is necessary for the male determination.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the autosomes determine traits like height, not sex.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the sex determination is localized to one specific pair.
